chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the Imam is present at the funeral, he is the most rightful of the people to perform the prayer upon it.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: The prayer (specifically Salat al-Janazah, funeral prayer)
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam, referring to the religious leader or authority figure

ai.seo_question: Who has the right to lead the funeral prayer when the Imam is present?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Imam's precedence in leading the funeral prayer, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that the highest-ranking religious authority assumes the role of Imamah in communal rites when present. It underscores the hierarchical structure of Shia religious leadership, where the Imam's presence validates and elevates the ritual, a concept deeply rooted in the broader Shia understanding of spiritual and temporal authority.
